subject: Request: procurement accommodation for card-only customer (prepay mismatch)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Singh <tara.singh@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-28T15:02:00Z
Subject: Quick recap + procurement question (Acme Health pilot)

Hi Tara — thanks again for the conversation today. Good to meet you and the Acme team. Recap and next steps from our side: 

- Pilot scope: 2 seats, sandbox access, up to ~500k tokens/mo for 3 months
- Primary success criteria: latency <250ms p95 and integration with your redaction pipeline
- Technical follow-ups: I'll share the infra diagram and the quantized model profile (attaching estimate).

Procurement question (important pathing item): during the call you mentioned procurement prefers vendors to go through your Azure Marketplace image; if we aren't on the marketplace there is a prepay requirement and no PO route. Can you confirm whether Acme would consider: 

A) credit card payments with monthly invoicing for the pilot (card-only) — customer ops can process card payments quickly, or
B) a prepay arrangement (wire) if card is not allowed, or
C) fast-track marketplace onboarding for the pilot (we can prioritize this but it usually takes 4–6 weeks).

If card-only is acceptable on your side, we can request an exception on our billing terms to accept a single-card monthly billing for the pilot while marketplace onboarding proceeds. If prepay is mandatory (and Acme won't do PO), please share the exact prepay amount and who from procurement I should engage with.

Attaching: pricing_estimate_v1.pdf (pilot quote).

Thanks — I’ll loop in finance/legal for any exception requests once you confirm.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Attachments: pricing_estimate_v1.pdf

From: Tara Singh <tara.singh@acmehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-29T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick recap + procurement question (Acme Health pilot)

Hi Soojin — quick clarifying note from procurement: our standard vendor policy is: vendors onboarded through the Azure Marketplace can be billed via marketplace invoicing (no prepay). For vendors not on the marketplace we require a prepayment equal to the first 3 months of committed spend; we do not issue POs for ad-hoc vendor card charges. For small pilots we sometimes make exceptions but only with finance approval.

For the pilot you outlined, procurement says Acme would prefer card-only (corporate card) but Finance will not sign off on card charges to a vendor if Procurement's system flags the vendor as "not marketplace" — that triggers the prepay requirement. We are trying to avoid the 4–6 week marketplace onboarding. 

Contacts: you can reach our finance approver Mark Haynes (mark.haynes@acmehealth.com) and Procurement Lead Priya Rao (priya.rao@acmehealth.com). Happy to set a short three-way call to surface the exact language needed for an exception.

Thanks,
Tara
Director, Product Integrations | Acme Health

Subject: Fwd: procurement nuance — Acme Health (asking for exception)

Marissa / Marcus / Rishi — forwarding procurement's note. TL;DR: Acme is card-first but their procurement system marks non-marketplace vendors for prepay, which blocks card flow. They want a short exception so they can use corporate card (monthly) for a 3-month pilot while we complete marketplace onboarding.

Customer impact: if we force prepay the pilot is unlikely to start — they explicitly said procurement won't accept PO or ad-hoc card charges without the vendor flagged as marketplace. They gave finance/procurement contacts (Mark & Priya).

Options I see: 
1) Approve an exception to accept corporate card monthly billing for a time-boxed pilot (30–90 days) with documented risk acceptance and a capped spend limit (suggest $50k cap for pilot). This is lowest friction for customer.
2) Require prepay (wire) per their policy — likely kills timeline; may still be acceptable if they can route funds quickly.
3) Accelerate marketplace onboarding — preferred long-term but 4–6 weeks, too slow for their pilot schedule.

If we approve 1), Finance/legal will want: short MSA addendum or one-page billing addendum, a capped spend, and a repayment/chargeback process documented. I can coordinate with Tara to get Mark/Priya on a call.

Requesting: quick decision whether we can make a temporary card-only accommodation for pilot (recommend yes with $50k cap). If yes, I’ll prepare the addendum and loop Legal/Finance for signoff.

Thanks,
Soojin
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_msa_draft.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-02T09:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: procurement nuance — Acme Health (asking for exception)

Thanks for the clear write-up, Soojin. I agree we should be pragmatic here — pilot wins frequently drive expansion. Approve a time-limited card-only accommodation with controls: 

- Cap pilot spend at $50,000
- 90-day maximum window
- Customer must sign the one-page Billing Addendum and accept that we can pause access if charges are disputed/unpaid
- Legal to review the addendum; Finance to accept residual risk and document the approval (Finance ticket #FIN-7842)

Marcus / Rishi: can you pick this up? Marcus, can your team produce the addendum template and Finance signoff checklist? Rishi, please confirm we can enforce the spend cap and that billing will be set to monthly card capture.

Soojin: please schedule a 30-min call with Tara + Mark + Priya + our Finance rep once Marcus/Rishi confirm. Also attach the screenshot of their policy you referenced (screenshot-prepay-policy.png) when you follow up.

—Marissa
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference
